title: The capture of Rome by the Visigoths
subject: histoire
description: In August 410, Alaric's Visigoths sacked Rome for three days. For the first time in eight centuries, an enemy army enters the Eternal City.

hero.hook: In 410, Rome fell. And with it, the idea of ​​an invincible empire.

blocks.text: In August **410**, the unimaginable happens. Led by their king **Alaric**, the **Visigoths**, a Germanic people, forced the gates of Rome. For the first time since the Gallic sack of **390 BC.**, almost **800 years ago**, an enemy army plundered the Eternal City.
Rome is no longer the political capital of the Empire, but it remains its symbolic heart. This shock reveals a truth that no one wanted to see: the Roman West was dying.

At the beginning of the 5th century, the Western Roman Empire lacked money and soldiers. To maintain the borders, he multiplied treaties of the  type: so-called “barbarian” peoples settled on the territory in exchange for military service. The Roman machine still holds up, but it depends on those it once struggled to contain. [[The Roman foedus]]

In **402**, the Western emperor  abandons Rome for , a city in Italy protected by its marshes. While the court goes underground, the Roman aristocracy continues to live as if nothing had changed. Real power shifted towards generals of Germanic origin. [[Honorius]] [[Ravenna]]
When the fall of “Rome” was announced, Honorius panicked: he thought they were talking about his favorite chicken, named as such. Relieved, they say, to learn that it was “only” about the city.

is not a savage from nowhere. Former officer in the Roman army, pushed westward by , a nomadic people from Asia, he wants land and an official title for his people. Faced with Ravenna's contempt, he uses Rome as a hostage. Two sieges, ransoms, then the assault. [[Alaric I]] [[The Huns]]

blocks.caption: Alaric I, king of the Visigoths and former Roman officer.

blocks.text: On **August 24, 410**, the Salaria gate opens. The looting lasts **three days**. A Christian of  faith (a current which did not see Christ as equal to God the Father), Alaric orders respect for the asylum of churches. Real violence, but not total destruction: he wants to be the heir of Rome, not the gravedigger. [[Arian]]
According to legend, when he died, his men diverted the Busento River to bury Alaric and his treasure, then returned the water to its bed.

sections.title: The Shock and The City of God

blocks.text: From Palestine, , a Father of the Church, exclaims: “In a single city, the entire universe has perished. » The pagans accuse Christianity of having weakened Rome. To respond, **Saint Augustine** writes : the earthly empires pass away; the Church remains. [[Saint Jerome]] [[The City of God]]

sections.title: The shift towards the Middle Ages

blocks.text: The Visigoths eventually settled in Aquitaine, then in Hispania (present-day Spain). They did not destroy all of classical culture: they became its smugglers, mixing Roman law, Christian faith and Germanic traditions.
The **410** bag remains the break in the memories. It is not yet the administrative end of the Empire, but it is the end of the illusion. Medieval Europe begins in the rubble of a myth.
In **410**, Rome fell for the first time in **800 years**. Visigoths trained in the Roman style plundered there for three days. The clash sets the stage for **476** and medieval Europe.
